checks.evidence: Six candidates now cover unit arithmetic, hosted inventory, label rendering, offline catalogue comparison/stack sums and no-account persistent tracking. New strong candidates were found by an independent wider web search; the three-query official final bundle is genuine but broad and star-ranked, not exhaustive.

Independent anonymous public API reread confirmed all six archived/default-branch commit/license values against hash-bound snapshots. Push, default commit and release remain separate signals; maintenance is not inferred from star updated_at. Canonical snapshot age classifications now match: nutrition-label inactive, SupplementTracker and stack active; final report distinguishes these machine labels from unverified ongoing support and quality.

All six actual adoption findings remain unknown. Historical 2022 individual spreadsheet anecdotes show a workflow exists, not 2026 prevalence, developer demand, conversion or growth. Publication is an experiment, not observed adoption.

wger LICENSE.txt corrected and verified; kleerer NOTICE directly confirms layered AGPL/restricted methodology/data terms. stack API license is UNKNOWN despite README MIT statement, so reuse permission remains unresolved. No upstream code/data is copied; all six security findings stay unknown.

The final report accepts spreadsheet+NIH and commercial-site-only as sufficient personal-use alternatives. kleerer materially overlaps offline comparison/totals, stack fits persistent tracking; build is limited to authorized publication of existing independently authored transient manual-input functions and a consistent embedding contract, not proven superiority, novelty or market need.

Official collector and transport adapter hashes match receipts; adapter only replaces urlopen and preserves parsing/time/field/error/write behavior. Four original candidate snapshots plus two added candidates were independently API-checked; original inventory search nine names and final comparator search first ten names/count174 reread match. Final report SHA verified and this review binds it.

challenges.challenge: A spreadsheet with NIH records already solves personal inventory and arithmetic; does publishing another repository mainly reflect sunk cost?
challenges.resolution: Report explicitly accepts that alternative and limits this decision to user-authorized source publication and browser embedding of narrow own functions already verified locally. Developer demand and acquisition value remain unknown; no full application, persistent tracker or eight duplicate repositories is justified. Lack of useful reuse/referrals should reduce maintenance rather than expand scope.

challenges.challenge: The original shortlist missed offline no-account competitors and could have selected account/server constraints to favor build.
challenges.resolution: kleerer and stack now have canonical official API snapshots and material coverage is admitted. kleerer overlaps comparison/stack sums; extraction feasibility is not tested and not ruled out. stack provides persistent stock/export. Narrow transient label functions are the current chosen contract, not a claim these projects are deficient or inferior.

challenges.challenge: Can competitor licenses and security claims support MIT reuse or a safety finding?
challenges.resolution: No upstream implementation/data is copied. kleerer layered NOTICE is acknowledged, stack README/API license ambiguity is unresolved, mathjs mixed components and wger data/documentation rights are distinguished. All security and actual adoption remain unknown; this admission pass is not a medical or security certification.

challenges.challenge: Could a curl adapter or hand-written links fabricate official collector evidence?
challenges.resolution: Unchanged canonical collectors run under runpy; transport accepts only public API GETs and returns HTTP entity bytes, preserving HTTPError semantics including release404. Script/adapter hashes and all six candidate API key fields matched; a final search first10/count174 matched independently. URL query and report hashes are bound by the canonical validator.
